customization.summary: Deployment unattested. Adapter talks HTTP to an existing AGENT_SANDBOX_URL or, by default, auto-spawns the repository FastAPI/uvicorn server as a host subprocess. That fallback is not Kubernetes-SIGs controller/CRD provisioning or managed GKE isolation. Official Kubernetes deployments allow image/resource/storage/network configuration; GKE offers a managed controller add-on on an operator-configured cluster. Saved results must not be assigned a security ranking.

features.notes: Official Sandbox/SandboxTemplate podTemplate selects a container image. Adapter sends no image and does not create templates/claims; auto_spawn uses host Python. Repository YAML/image is deployment intent, not evidence that it ran.

A chosen image can bundle dependencies and runtime installation depends on permission/egress. Saved report observes preinstalled packages and pip availability, not installing a new package. Auto-spawn inherits the host runtime and network.

Official pod templates support requests/limits. Repository manifest requests 500m and limits 2 CPUs; adapter sends neither and auto-spawn sets no CPU constraint. Report's cost assumption of 2 vCPU does not attest effective allocation.

Official pod templates support memory requests/limits. Repository manifest requests 1Gi and limits 4Gi; adapter sends neither. Saved allocation workload reaching 2000MB is not a 4Gi limit or allocation measurement. Actual deployment limits unknown.

A real GKE gVisor deployment can use supported GPUs for CUDA under version/model/driver constraints; microVM sandbox runtimes do not support GPUs per reviewed GKE docs. Adapter/manifest request no accelerator and report contains no GPU inventory. No accelerator access is attested here.

Official GKE add-on manages ingress/egress policies and permits template customization. Auto-spawn installs no network policy. Report observed DNS/HTTP allowed and metadata URL failure, which does not prove an enforced isolation policy or identify the deployment.

Upstream supports persistent storage surviving Pod restarts when configured. Local fallback uses a shared temporary base directory removed in teardown; per-run cleanup is a no-op. No PVC/mount/retention attestation in report or local template.

Upstream provides stable stateful Sandbox identity/lifecycle. This adapter targets one HTTP server/base directory with no claim/session allocation. A five-turn loop inside one execution does not prove independently isolated cross-request sessions.

Saved Python workloads ran through /execute. Repository server executes arbitrary commands with asyncio.create_subprocess_shell in a working directory; auto-spawn imposes no kernel/container boundary. Measured command execution is not measured sandbox isolation.

HTTP upload/download are implemented, but the saved roundtrip stdout says 20 output bytes with SHA 03f8b5a6985317bb443711cf59982832808ed02a2a2b2c2e7c07bd702ac081e9 while collected artifact is 35 bytes with SHA 1093d1f916b518786a39c26266690572a4dfb9b7273ca21cf923acd9e42fa394. This is not a verified byte-faithful roundtrip. Adapter collects only two candidate paths.

Official deployments route HTTP through a Sandbox Router and production direct/Gateway connections. Operator configures services, exposure and authentication; no automatic public preview URL. Local port 8888 is an execution API, not proof of application-port preview support.

Upstream is a Kubernetes CRD/controller installed on an operator cluster; GKE alternatively manages the controller add-on. Adapter can run its local server but does not provision either deployment. The saved deployment remains unattested.

GKE can use customer-managed keys for node boot disks and attached Persistent Disks/Filestore with explicit KMS/IAM/StorageClass setup. This is infrastructure/storage-specific, not an Agent Sandbox API guarantee; control-plane disks cannot use CMEK. No key configured by adapter or attested in report.

pricing.model: No universal Kubernetes-SIGs per-execution tariff; pay for deployed infrastructure, warm pools, router/controller capacity, storage and networking. GKE Agent Sandbox adds no feature fee; normal GKE pricing applies.

rates.resource: GKE Agent Sandbox incremental feature fee
GKE cluster management before eligible credits
Deployment CPU, memory, GPU, storage and network

pricing.limitations: Deployment unattested, so no measured cloud cost. Saved $0.000072/second and 2-vCPU/4-GB inputs have no bill/SKU provenance. GKE Standard nodes use Compute Engine per-second billing with one-minute minimum; general-purpose Autopilot uses requested Pod resources in one-second increments with no duration minimum; selected hardware uses node-based billing plus management premium. Warm pool idle capacity and cluster/router/storage costs cannot be omitted. GKE monthly eligible cluster-fee credit is $74.40 per billing account, not free workload compute. No historical increase or security ranking asserted.
